historical_source.title: Lectures on the Ising and Potts models on the hypercubic lattice
historical_source.author: Hugo Duminil-Copin
historical_source.locator: PDF p. 93, printed p. 94, Section 7, Conjecture 6 and equation (7.1)
historical_source.verbatim_short_quote: Prove that the three-dimensional Ising model is non-trivial
historical_source.definition_quote: If g(beta) tends to 0 as beta approaches beta_c, the field is said to be trivial. Otherwise, it is said to be non-trivial.
historical_source.exact_math_interpretation: The notes define g(beta) as the spatial sum of the four-point Ursell function U4(0,x2,x3,x4) divided by chi(beta)^2 xi(beta)^d, and ask that g(beta) not tend to zero as beta increases to beta_c for the nearest-neighbor Ising model on Z^3. They also describe this in terms of failure of Wick factorization in the spin-field scaling limit.
historical_source.caveat: PDF extraction drops the final word after 'the four-dimensional Ising model is'; the 3D clause is intact. The source defines g without a minus sign although U4 is nonpositive, so nonvanishing is the convention-free property.

ranking: Tier 5, attempted_un in RANKING_2026-09-07.csv:542; this is historical, not proof of current openness.
status_reason: 2017 source states the conjecture; bounded 2026-10-10 public search found no primary rigorous proof of its 3D clause, but an absence of search results is not a definitive novelty audit. The similarly titled 2017 Rychkov-Simmons-Duffin-Zan paper uses conformal-bootstrap input rather than a lattice-to-scaling-limit proof.
distinct_related_result: Aizenman and Duminil-Copin, Annals of Mathematics 194 (2021), proves the 4D triviality clause, not the 3D nontriviality clause.
independent_route_relation: The finite-volume Lee-Yang criterion in CLAIMS.jsonl is not yet a reduction to the exact g(beta) statement.
